criterion: reworked control flow in an existing rule with no behaviour-pinning test
finding: The reworked watchdog fire rule applies to every role agent, so in the subagent fallback a hung subtask subagent is never parked any more.
why: GLOSSARY.md:76 defines a role agent as a subagent when no pane transport is found, the fallback has no team entry script and so never has a completion signal, and the new rule leaves an agent with no signal that is still running at work and re-arms its watchdog. That replaces the old 'Silent → stop the child's task and take the invoking skill's park/fail path' and breaks PRD AC-001, which says a run with no pane transport behaves as before. skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md:40 now contradicts itself: 'a fire follows that section' against 'Watchdog fires and the probe finds the subagent silent → mark it parked(timeout)'. Line 35 has the same scope problem: 'the contact agent arms, fires and disarms the watchdog, whoever asked for the agent' asks the top-level session to arm a watchdog for a nested role subagent that it did not start and cannot stop. No test pins this text (INV-082 REPORT.md: 'No gate or test reads DELEGATION.md's spawn-rule, watchdog or tier text').
fix: Change 'For a role agent' at DELEGATION.md:35, :37, :38 and :39 to 'For a pane role agent', so a subagent role agent keeps the old spawner-armed rule and the silent-means-park rule, and make the autopilot:40 fire wording follow the same split.
evidence: DELEGATION.md:38 '+For a role agent, the contact agent reads the agent's completion signal (the file the team entry script writes when it accepts the agent's finished message) first: present, the agent finished. Absent and the agent alive, the agent stays working: the contact agent reads its output and re-arms'; GLOSSARY.md:76 'A pane agent when a pane transport is found and the pane switch does not say subagent; otherwise a subagent'; contract Acceptance 'With no pane transport or the switch set back, a run behaves as it did before this feature' (PRD AC-001)

criterion: acceptance bullet: BEHAVIORS.md short form names the condition and both branches of the rule
finding: The short form defines role work as writing 'files', which is wider than the full rule's 'a plugin artifact'.
why: The short form reaches every repository, so an agent that reads only the block will start a helper that writes evidence files (for example a runner) as a pane agent, against DELEGATION.md:24 and PRD AC-040.
fix: Use the full rule's words in the short form, 'writes a plugin artifact, code or a ledger', and make the same change in CHANGELOG.md:71.
evidence: BEHAVIORS.md:16 'start a role agent (it writes files, code or a ledger, or returns a gate verdict) as a pane agent'; DELEGATION.md:24 'An agent that writes a plugin artifact, code or a ledger, or returns a gate verdict, does role work'; CHANGELOG.md:70-71 'an agent that writes files, code or a ledger'

finding: The seam-test for the doctrine row checks no text the slice adds: its only own check, `grep -c 'suite/build runners'`, also prints 1 at base 83372fd.
why: Plan D-36 names 0014's text checks as the seam-test of the row "`DELEGATION` doctrine: `Model tiers` carve-out and `stall-watchdog` rules". The other text check, `grep -c 'pane-agent rule'`, covers only the spawn-rules row. So no check fails when the carve-out (:54), the contact-agent fire rule (:39), park and resume (:41) or the wait job (:42) is missing. Each of these phrases counts 0 at 83372fd and 1 at 88831ae.
fix: Add static greps to the 0014 Verification table that each print 1 at head and 0 at base, for example `A team pattern the human writes`, `Park and resume`, `The wait job` and `completion signal` in DELEGATION.md. Keep the `suite/build runners` grep as the check that the runner arm stays.
evidence: Contract Verification: "`grep -c 'suite/build runners' DELEGATION.md` prints 1 | ... with the row above, the seam-test of §14 row "`DELEGATION` doctrine: `Model tiers` carve-out and `stall-watchdog` rules"". Base text (old DELEGATION.md:106): "Arm every spawn whose child can run past ~15 min (subtask executors, suite/build runners, provisioning gates):". Counts checked with `git show <rev>:DELEGATION.md | grep -c`: 'suite/build runners' gives base=1, head=1; 'A team pattern the human writes', 'Park and resume', 'The wait job' and 'completion signal' each give base=0, head=1.

finding: The role-agent fire branch covers a present signal and an absent signal with a live agent. It has no branch for an absent signal with a dead agent.
why: A pane agent that exits without sending its finished message matches neither branch. Autopilot step 5 parks only 'the subagent', so it does not cover this case either. Inference: the job supervisor's exited message may cover it later, but the watchdog text does not say so.
fix: Add 'Absent and the agent gone: mark it lost and take the invoking skill's park path' to the On fire clause.
evidence: DELEGATION.md:38 "present, the agent finished. Absent and the agent alive, the agent stays working"; skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md:40 "Watchdog fires and the probe finds the subagent silent → mark it `parked(timeout)`"
